newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore Dec bank credit rises 16.5 pct on year.
newsitem.headline: Singapore Dec bank credit rises 16.5 pct on year.

text.p: Bank credit to non-bank customers (in billions of Singapore dollars):

The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) said in its monthly report that bank credit expanded at a faster rate of 16.5 percent year-on-year in December, compared with 15.6 percent in November, after five months of moderate growth.
The improvement in credit growth was fairly broad-based.
Credit extended to non-bank financial institutions and the commerce sector rose to 15.1 percent and 10.6 percent respectively in December, from 12.1 percent and 9.6 percent in November.
Growth of loans to the building and construction sector, including housing loans, rebounded to 22.3 percent, after sliding for the last three consecutive months.
Growth of loans to the manufacturing sector also firmed at around 11 percent in December.

But growth in loans to the transport sector and personal loans slowed. Loan growth to the transport sector moderated to 20.2 percent, compared with 25.1 percent in November, and to professional and private individuals declined to 19.9 percent, from 22.4 percent, the MAS said.
